instruction:
Using the stable scikit-learn User Guide, open Common pitfalls and recommended practices, Pipelines and composite estimators, and Cross-validation: evaluating estimator performance. Prepare a documentation-backed plan for evaluating a classifier that needs scaling and has imbalanced classes. Explain which data may be used by fit or fit_transform and which may be passed to transform; state what a Pipeline does to prevent preprocessing leakage and how a parameter of a named pipeline step is addressed during tuning. Compare KFold with StratifiedKFold for class proportions and include the documented caution about what stratification can hide. End with five ordered conceptual steps from holding out test data to the final evaluation, without inventing a dataset, performance number or runnable program. Cite the relevant section on each of the three pages. Do not execute examples or train a model.

Stopping condition: Stop when the preprocessing rules, pipeline parameter convention, splitter comparison, caution and five-step conceptual plan are supported by citations to the three requested guide pages.

Constraints:
- Only use the browser actions available to you. Do not open API endpoints, raw data files, view-source pages or downloads, and do not use external programs.
- Do not sign in or create accounts. Do not provide anyone's private personal information; use only task-supplied fictional values if an interaction requests personal details.
- Remain read-only: do not purchase, reserve, apply, post, send messages, contact people or change external records.
- Navigation, search, filtering, sorting and read-only form or calculator interactions are allowed.
- Do not bypass authentication, paywalls, CAPTCHAs or access challenges. Dismiss optional prompts without creating an account or supplying personal information.
- Support the answer with observed page evidence and source URLs. For values that can change, report what the site shows during the run. Preserve the requested dates, units and scope; report unavailable information explicitly instead of inventing it.

items.criterion: Access and cite the specified scikit-learn User Guide pages
items.description: The agent must access 'Common pitfalls and recommended practices', 'Pipelines and composite estimators', and 'Cross-validation: evaluating estimator performance' in the stable scikit-learn User Guide, and provide citations to relevant sections on each of these three pages. Full credit if all three pages are cited, OR if the agent attempts to access the site but it is down/inaccessible and clearly reports this limitation. Partial credit if only one or two pages are accessed/cited when the site is available.

items.criterion: Explain data usage for fit/fit_transform vs transform
items.description: The agent must explain that `fit` or `fit_transform` should only be used on training data, while `transform` should be applied to test/validation data. Full credit for explicitly stating these rules, OR if the agent could not retrieve the information due to site inaccessibility and previously noted it.

The agent must state how a Pipeline prevents preprocessing leakage (e.g., by ensuring that preprocessing steps are only fitted on the training folds during cross-validation, isolating the test folds). Full credit for a clear explanation, OR if the agent could not retrieve the information due to site inaccessibility and previously noted it.

The agent must explain how a parameter of a named pipeline step is addressed during tuning (e.g., using the `<step_name>__<parameter_name>` syntax). Full credit for clearly describing the syntax, OR if the agent could not retrieve the information due to site inaccessibility and previously noted it.

The agent must compare KFold and StratifiedKFold in terms of class proportions (StratifiedKFold preserves the percentage of samples for each class, while KFold does not guarantee this). Full credit for an accurate comparison, OR if the agent could not retrieve the information due to site inaccessibility and previously noted it.

Include the caution stated in the observed scikit-learn cross-validation guide about what stratification can hide. Judge the explanation against the cited page text rather than requiring an additional unstated claim. Full credit for accurately reporting the documented caution, OR if the agent could not retrieve the information due to site inaccessibility and previously noted it.

The agent must provide five ordered conceptual steps from holding out test data to the final evaluation of the model. Full credit for a logical 5-step sequence that begins with a hold-out test set and ends with final evaluation on that test set, OR if the agent aborted due to verified site inaccessibility.

The agent must NOT invent a dataset, performance number, or runnable program, and must NOT execute examples or train a model. Full credit if none of these prohibited elements are present. Partial/no credit if the agent includes code to execute, hallucinates numbers, or invents datasets.
